title: Two-Step Equations: From One Step to Two
preview: Open the file cabinet with one-step equations, then thin-slice into two-step equations. Each step varies one detail at a time.

body.goal: Students bridge from one-step to two-step equation solving by noticing that a two-step is just two one-steps in a row.
body.launch: Run the warm-up first ('Open the File Cabinet') so one-step solving is fresh in their hands. Then start the thin-slice — the new wrinkle is just one extra move.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up with one-step equations before the slice begins.

prerequisiteSteps.teacherNote: Switch to multiplication — undone by division.

steps.teacherNote: First two-step. Some groups will subtract first, some will divide first. Let both happen — discuss order at the consolidation.
Same structure, just bigger numbers — confirms the procedure.
Division instead of multiplication. Same logic — undo addition first, then undo division.
The grouped one. Push: which 'undo' goes first now? Why?

body.consolidation: After the slice, ask: 'In a two-step equation, which move do you undo first? Why?' Pull out the rule: undo addition/subtraction before multiplication/division — order of operations in reverse.
